verdict.rationale: Turso documents a local database option: 'local database file, no server needed (recommended)'. It describes its engine as embedded, running 'entirely in your process' and usable 'Offline'. One community user also reports using it locally. However, the docs never say this local mode needs no account or token, and they never mention CI test usage. missing for 10: explicit documentation that local use needs no account or API key, documented CI/test-pipeline usage, independent hands-on corroboration of offline keyless operation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the same engine locally and keylessly — no account or cloud dependency — for offline development and CI tests

citations.quote: Local Turso database — local database file, no server needed (recommended)
They are fully SQLite-compatible — they open existing SQLite files — and run entirely in your process, no server needed
An embedded database engine that goes anywhere. Offline, in the browser, or on-device.
I've been using it locally and with their hosted offering for awhile now and it's rock solid
